item.title: Battlefield 6 has come under fire from fans after its latest battle pass was found to include new character skins with some pretty clear design flaws.
item.description:
Battlefield 6 has come under fire from fans after its latest battle pass was found to include new character skins with some pretty clear design flaws.
The first that stands out is the soldier wearing some kind of Batman mask, but minus the ears. He has five pistols attached to the chest pockets of his tac vest, for when you positively, absolutely have to go Shiva mode on some clowns. “Because switching to your pistol, secondary pistol, tertiary pistol, quartenary (sic) pistol, and quinary pistol is faster than reloading, soldier!” one Reddit poster joked.
💀 BRO IS CARRYING 5 PISTOLS! WHO APPROVED THIS SKIN? 😭#Battlefield6 https://t.co/b6o94OkV1o
Illogical pistol placement isn’t the only thing weirding fans out. Some are convinced some of the skins were actually created with generative AI, after noticing weird spelling errors and other inconsistencies. One of the skins has a patch that says “secuty” on it, which is presumably supposed to say “security.”
Secuty 😭 It's AI #Battlefield6 https://t.co/8DVphghCSU
"I believe it’s almost impossible to deny anymore that EA/DICE is using AI for the skins in #Battlefield6,” said one X / Twitter poster. “At least in the concept phase — and then anything that looks even remotely 'cool' just gets rubber-stamped.”
IGN has asked EA for comment.
Another skin features a bomb disposal juggernaut with thick body armor and a completely exposed head, like a cheeky little turtle poking out of its shell. Imagine aura farming when the shrapnel starts flying. It doesn’t help that he’s carrying magazines for small game hunting rifles that don’t exist in Battlefield 6.
“Fps .22s probably take like 2 full mags to kill someone,” one X / Twitter user said. “Not to mention he's carrying super finicky mags for a .22 varmint rifle,” joked another.
While it's possible that these skin issues are the result of human error, fans aren't giving DICE the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps that shouldn't come as much of a surprise; AI is perhaps the hottest topic in the video game industry, and with the likes of Fortnite developer Epic Games going all-in on generative AI, there is an intense scrutiny and a healthy dose of skepticism around video game assets that contain clear errors, particularly when they cost money to buy.
Elsewhere, fans are feeling misled over the inclusion of more whacky cosmetics. As well as a reactive weapon skin, there are crossover cosmetics with other EA series, allowing Battlefield 6 players to do some Dead Space cosplay. These land ahead of the Battlefield 6 Dead Space event.
It’s not quite Nicki Minaj, but the inclusion of these skins goes back on what the developers said prior to launch. Developers at DICE had gone on the record to say Battlefield 6 won’t feature goofy, immersion breaking skins.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Rockstar has promised that its next game following GTA 6 won’t take as long to come out, although it failed to hint at what it might be.
item.description:
Rockstar has promised that its next game following GTA 6 won’t take as long to come out, although it failed to hint at what it might be.
GTA 6 finally launches in November, eight years after the release of its last game, Red Dead Redemption 2. In a new report by Bloomberg detailing the challenges Rockstar has faced during GTA 6’s development, company leadership said whatever’s next won’t take as long because the work done for GTA 6 provides a foundation for following it up faster.
“The engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly,” Phil Hooker, co-head of development, said.
“I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content.”
“We foundationally changed a lot of stuff on this project,” co-head of development Aaron Garbut added. “But now it’s done, and we’re not going to rip it apart.”
The question fans have is, what will Rockstar’s next game be? Bloomberg compares the release of GTA 6 to GTA 3, in that the first 3D GTA game paved the way for the quickfire release of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which launched a year later in 2002. Could Rockstar soon follow GTA 6 with another GTA game, perhaps focused on another city?
Many hope and expect Rockstar to make Red Dead Redemption 3, although Rockstar itself hasn’t indicated it has plans to do so. A year ago, Rockstar Games co-founder and former lead writer Dan Houser said RDR3 “will probably happen.” In 2023, Roger Clark, who played Arthur Morgan, the main playable protagonist of Red Dead Redemption 2, said he was “certain” fans would see Red Dead Redemption 3 “one day,” but qualified that statement by saying he had no idea when that would be. Clark also ruled out the return of Arthur Morgan in the game, should it come to be. If you’ve played Red Dead Redemption 2, this might seem like stating the obvious, but there’s always the chance Rockstar may consider another prequel of some kind.
“I’m certain we will see Red Redemption 3 one day,” Clark said. “When that will be — I have absolutely no idea. Don’t count on Arthur’s involvement either. His story has been told, I feel.”
In a subsequent interview with IGN, Clark expanded on his thoughts: “Yeah, that got really picked up! I would have thought that was obvious though. Wouldn’t you? And it’s not like I have any insider information whatsoever, but of course there’s going to be another Red Dead. It sold over 60 million copies!”
He continued: “Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Take-Two said it himself. He said GTA and Red Dead are prominent franchises for Rockstar Games and that they will be returning to them in the future. So there’s no doubt there will be another Red Dead. But if Arthur Morgan will be involved? I highly doubt it, to be honest. And I think it’s going to be quite some time before we even see a snifter of anything new Red Dead related. I have no idea how it would pan out, but I wouldn’t bet on Arthur being a part of it.”
In April this year, Hollywood star Jack Black revealed the character he’d love to play in Red Dead Redemption 3, should Rockstar make the game: Jack Black. In lieu of a Red Dead Redemption movie, which Black said he’d very much love to star in if the opportunity ever came his way, the Bowser actor would love to star in Red Dead Redemption 3. And it turns out there’s a character called Jack Black he’d love to play.
"Red Dead Redemption 2 takes place around the turn of the century, right?" Black told Polygon while promoting The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. "There was a character around that time named Jack Black, who wrote an autobiography called You Can't Win. I would kinda like to play Jack Black in Red Dead Redemption 3."
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Activision has confirmed the global release times and preload details for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launches in various parts over the coming weeks.
item.description:
Activision has confirmed the global release times and preload details for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launches in various parts over the coming weeks.
Modern Warfare 4 (full game including Multiplayer) officially launches on October 23 across all platforms, but you’ll be able to play the campaign a week before that with Early Access, which kicks off on October 16. DMZ, Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode, is available from October 20.
Whether you’re playing Modern Warfare 4 on PC, PS5, Xbox Series consoles, or Nintendo Switch 2, this post will cover everything you need to know about getting those boots on the ground: release times, preload details, Early Access launch, and more.
As I said above, Modern Warfare 4 officially comes out on October 23, but what time you’ll get access depends on whether you have Early Access and what platform you plan to play on.
Modern Warfare 4 players on PC will be able to jump on at midnight local time on the morning of October 23. Wherever you’re based, the game will unlock at midnight. If it doesn’t trigger straight away, fully close and exit Steam — a relaunch should trigger it.
Campaign Early Access for Modern Warfare 4 begins on October 16, 2026, for players who digitally preorder the Standard Digital Edition or Vault Edition of the game. For people who bought physical, there’s no Early Access for preorders of the Standard Edition.
Additionally, players who preordered will get Early Access to DMZ mode, which kicks off on October 20.
Here’s a look at the Modern Warfare 4 editions:
Preload for Modern Warfare 4 will begin rolling out on October 14 at 9pm PT. Here’s how that looks for other regions:
During setup, you can choose which content to download, including whether to install Warzone alongside Modern Warfare 4. The new version of Warzone will not be available until the launch of Season 1.
Xbox players should be able to circumvent regional restrictions with the New Zealand trick, where they change their in-game timezone to New Zealand in the settings, tricking their console into letting them pre-install and play early.
According to the official Modern Warfare 4 system requirements, the game will need 115GB of available SSD space on PC. Console versions may vary — and it’ll depend what content you decide to download — but they’ll likely be somewhat similar.

item.title: The cuts and studio shutdowns continue at Ubisoft, this time with layoffs hitting the developer of Skull and Bones and the closure of Trials maker RedLynx.
item.description:
The cuts and studio shutdowns continue at Ubisoft, this time with layoffs hitting the developer of Skull and Bones and the closure of Trials maker RedLynx.
GamesIndustry.biz reported that Finnish studio RedLynx will close down, with up to 52 people losing their jobs. Meanwhile, Ubisoft Singapore, developer of pirate game Skull and Bones, will lose 70 staff. In a statement, Ubisoft insisted Ubisoft Singapore “remains an important part of Ubisoft’s global production organization.” GI said 70 staff represented around a fifth of Singapore’s total headcount, which suggests 280 staff are left.
Skull & Bones suffered a notoriously choppy development that stretched out over years. After a series of delays, it eventually launched early 2024 with a $70 price tag that Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot justified by describing Skull & Bones as a "quadruple-A game." Year 3 Season 2, titled Crimson Waters, launched in August.
RedLynx, meanwhile, was gobbled up by Ubisoft in 2011 having enjoyed enormous success with the likes of Trials 2, Trials HD, and Trials Evolution, games that challenged players to navigate increasingly difficult side-scrolling courses on a bike. But after the launch of Trials Rising in 2019, RedLynx became a Ubisoft support studio.
It’s a sad end for RedLynx, once one of the most high-profile Xbox Live Arcade developers in the business. I have many fond memories of playing Trials HD and Trials Evolution on lunch breaks with colleagues at my previous stomping ground, Eurogamer, where we’d laugh and shout our way to the finish line in local competitive multiplayer. Trials was Infuriating — of course it was, it’s called Trials — but so much fun.
Ubisoft is of course still cutting costs left, right, and center across the business as it reorganizes itself into a leaner operation focused on fewer games. Multiple studios have closed down in recent years, many staff have lost their jobs, and games have been canceled.
Most recently, Natalie Francis was appointed Studio MD of Massive Entertainment, with Thomas Andrén’s becoming General Manager for Ubisoft’s Creative Network. Massive Entertainment, based in Malmö, Sweden, is currently leading the development of The Division 2 and The Division 3, operates development on the Snowdrop game engine, and works on Ubisoft Connect.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak, has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB.
item.description:
The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak, has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB.
Last year, an adorable, cheap co-op game known as Peak blew up on Steam. In the game, players unite with their friends to pass through a wide variety of deadly obstacles in order to climb absurdly tall mountains. They must use the power of friendship and a handful of tools to overcome the odds, often resulting in hilarious deaths, injuries, and hijinks. As of August 2025, Peak has sold over 10 million copies, partially thanks to the fact it only costs $8 and is an easy sell to a group of friends.
It seems like the game will likely only continue to grow its audience, as the ESRB has rated Peak for PS5. Historically, ESRB leaks are incredibly accurate, so it seems like only a matter of time before an official announcement is made. As of right now, it's unclear if Peak will also come to Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2, but it would be surprising if this remained console exclusive to PS5.
Unfortunately for new players, Peak ended its post-launch support earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't expect the game to receive any significant content after it releases on console. It's also unclear if it will enjoy the same exceptionally low price when it does hit consoles, but it would be surprising if the team behind the game changed it. Following the game's release, the team noted that there's a psychology behind pricing a game that low.
“We had this joke of, like, 'How much is a game really?'" said Peak co-creator Nick Kaman. "In a player’s mind, what does it mean to spend five bucks? Well, that’s five bucks. But six bucks? Well, that’s still five bucks. Four bucks is also kind of five bucks. Three bucks is two bucks. And two bucks is basically free. So we’ve got these tiers: You know, twelve bucks… that’s ten bucks. But thirteen bucks is fifteen bucks. And we found that eight bucks is still five bucks. It doesn’t become ten bucks. Seven ninety nine, that’s five bucks, right? So, eight bucks going to five bucks is the biggest differential we could find in pricing, so we found it very optimal.”
It's unclear when an official announcement might follow, but if there's an ESRB rating, it typically means that the game isn't too far away from a release.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Razer just dropped three new Pokémon-inspired headsets.
The new colorways, which form part of Pokémon’s ongoing 30th anniversary celebrations, are for two of the tech company’s most popular gaming headsets: the Kraken V4 and the Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed. In typical collab fashion, each design is based on a specific Pokémon. This particular collection puts the spotlight on Sylveon, Charizard, and Lucario.
The headsets are now available directly from Razer and Target, though with a significant markup at the latter.
The Razer Kraken V4 is getting the Sylveon Edition treatment. This wired headset sports a retractable mic, 7.1 surround sound, and customizable RGB with Razer Chroma. The Sylveon design is all about the pastels, with an image of Sylveon printed on the headband and soft blue details on the earcups. Razer’s own official listing calls the new edition “coquette-style.”
The base model headset costs $79.99, and the Sylveon Edition is currently listed at Razer for the same price.
The Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed headset is getting two new colorways based on some of the coolest Pokemon, Charizard and Lucario. This is a slightly higher-end headset tuned specifically for esports, with the standard edition priced at $20 more than the Kraken V4. It’s also lighter, weighing 270g to the Kraken’s 300g. Razer boasts a low-latency wireless connection supported by 2.4GHz HyperSpeed technology and up to 70 hours of battery life.
The Charizard edition is colored in black and red flames with orange lining, while the Lucario model features vibrant blue earcubs and ink-like illustrations.
Razer Kraken V4 - Sylveon Edition
Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed - Lucario Edition
Razer Blackshark V3 X Hyperspeed - Charizard Edition
Razer has previously released a number of Pokémon-themed peripherals, including a general Pokémon line of accessories and the viral Gengar headset. It’s not surprising to see the two companies lock hands once again for the gaming giant’s 30th anniversary.
Meanwhile Target, which is selling the new Razer headsets at a significant markup, released an entire Pokémon anniversary collection earlier this summer.

item.title: We are just a little over 30 days until the release of GTA 6, which begs the question: will you be taking time off of work or school to play it?
item.description:
We are just a little over 30 days away from the release of GTA 6, which begs the question: Will you be taking time off of work or school to play it?
GTA 6 is one of the biggest pop culture events of the decade, if not in all of history, and as a result, it's expected to cause some disruption. In addition to fears that the game's highly-anticipated launch may create instability for ISPs and platform servers, many companies are also expected to have an irregular amount of employees calling out for the day. For months, fans on social media have been claiming they're putting in PTO requests well in advance of November to ensure they can have the game's release weekend available. So, will you be taking November 19 off? Let us know in the poll below, dear reader.
Economists have estimated that there will be a $1 billion loss in productivity during launch week due to people being absent from their jobs. A car tuning company known as Burger Motorsports has even announced that it will be closed on November 19, the day of the game's release, due to an excess of employees requesting that day off. The Australian government has also released some interesting PSAs, informing citizens about their rights when it comes to taking time off around the release of GTA 6.
The U.S. Army even offered soldiers four days of time off for the game's launch if they reenlist. NBA star Steven Adams also joked that the various sports leagues would see a drop in performance due to the release of GTA 6. Of course, Rockstar is ensuring that, regardless of performance, sports fans are hyper-aware of its upcoming game thanks to an unprecdented GTA 6-themed NBA regular season game in Miami and a blitz of advertising at the Hard Rock Stadium where the Miami Dolphins play.
It's likely we will see a slew of other companies joining in on the GTA 6 hype as the game's launch approaches. Rockstar Games is making sure the whole world knows that its highly-anticipated release is nearly here after multiple delays. A plethora of ads have been spotted in and around Miami, New York City, and Paris. Rockstar is also investing a boatload of cash into the game's music, as it has produced an album filled with original music from the likes of Cardi B, Travis Scott, and Keith Richards. The game's radio stations will also be hosted by major musicians like Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, and Bad Bunny, where they will play a variety of mainstream hits.
The 13-year wait for a new GTA game is nearly over as GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. A PC version is also rumored to release in the first quarter of 2027.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we can reveal a new gameplay trailer for Send in the Clown, the upcoming one-hour comedy RPG where players become history's least-appreciated clown as he tries to save a 12-year-old's birthday from her brat brother.
item.description:
As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we can reveal a new gameplay trailer for Send in the Clown, the upcoming one-hour comedy RPG where players become history's least-appreciated clown as he tries to save a 12-year-old's birthday from her brat brother.
Co-directors Nick Park and Jacques Mouledoux walk us through the latest look at Send in the Clown, focusing squarely on the game's climactic, one-and-only turn-based RPG battle.
Yes, the team built a whole battle system for just one fight, and all the roads that lead to it are pretty hilarious.
Players will step into the oversized shoes of Pockets as he tries to save Miranda's party from her brother Tad. To do so, he'll need to recruit characters and gather items, which will in turn unlock each character's unique ability.
For example, if he can teach a single dad how to dance, he'll unlock a dance troupe attack. If he helps hype up Miranda's friend Nasser, the team will be able to use the 'Be a Hero' move that protects an ally from damage. Lastly, if you are able to give a mother a break from watching her baby so she can lay be the pool, she will be able to throw said baby at an enemy for ultimate damage.
We also got a tease of other ways you can help turn the tide of the final battle in your favor, including finding Tad's baby photos, finding religion, and waking Nanna. Developer Mad Herons wouldn't reveal what would happen when you find those things, but the reward will surely be useful.
Send in the Clown is set to debut later this year on PC via Steam, and you can check out the demo right now.
For more from IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, check out our main guide that explains how to watch, what to expect, and more.
Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

item.title: Official K/DA accounts have been updated for the first time in six years. New profile and banner images continue to show the existing promotional art from the All Out era, now with the addition of hot pink flames. The reactivated accounts have also wiped existing posts, fueling rumors that the virtual girl group is gearing up for a comeback.
item.description:
Official K/DA accounts have been updated for the first time in six years. New profile and banner images continue to show the existing promotional art from the All Out era, now with the addition of hot pink flames. The reactivated accounts have also wiped existing posts, fueling rumors that the virtual girl group is gearing up for a comeback.
K/DA, which debuted at the 2018 League of Legends World Championship, consists of four League champions (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'Sa) voiced by international pop stars. The group’s first single, aptly called POP/STARS, was the first K-pop song by a girl group to receive RIAA Platinum certification in 2022. The early success of the girl group prompted the release of a full EP, All Out, in 2020.
Since then, the group has pretty much gone dark. K/DA skins still exist in-game, but there’s been no word on new music or performances. Until now.
I’m not asking for much. I just want to see a teaser from K/DA that’s as peak as this. https://t.co/gWU9yf04w9
An updated banner image continues to use promotional images from the All Out era, showing the main K/DA quartet alongside the era’s guest artist, Seraphine, who was a newly released champion at the time. As of October 13, however, those images also show the addition of hot pink and magenta flames.
Datamined leaks from earlier this year already raised hopes that the group would have some role in the current season of League of Legends. Details in a Wild Rift update, first spotted by SkinSpotlights, pointed to a potential “Firestarter” skin concept, as well as a new song registered on the ASCAP Repertory.
Other users have interpreted the purple smoke as a sign that K/DA is being added to Fortnite, which is currently using similarly colored imagery for its Fortnitemares event.
The question of K/DA’s return extends beyond Riot, as it also depends on the availability of the four singers associated with the group: Madison Beer, Soyeon, Miyeon, and Jaira Burns.
Online fan accounts recently started circulating the rumor that Beer would be leaving the group. The singer herself was asked about her return to K/DA during her recent Locket tour, saying: "I would love to. It’s not really up to me, although I wish it was. There actually was a conversation a few years ago about doing something again, but I don’t know what happened to it.”
Riot has yet to confirm any rumors about a K/DA comeback, let alone who the group currently includes. The League of Legends World Championship tournament is currently being hosted across the United States, with the Grand Final scheduled for November 14. Given that K/DA made its debut at the Worlds tournament, there’s a possibility we'll hear more over the course of this year's event.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.
item.description:
Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.
No doubt seeing the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved), Microsoft itself is keen to get in on the action in support of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goal of reaching 1 billion players per day.
Xbox has been tinkering with running Xbox and Xbox 360 games in browsers, and the Xbox Labs initiative is a formalization of those efforts that will see a small team of engineers playing with emerging technologies in order to find new ways for games new and old to be distributed and even created. And IGN understands that this won't just be an R&D effort; rather, Xbox Labs is tasked with shipping products – Sharma says, "We'll build in the open" – and getting gamers to engage with them.
I'd suggest thinking about it as a next phase of the backward compatibility efforts that started at Xbox over a decade ago, which the recent disc-to-digital program built on (which, side note, is a much more consumer-friendly path towards the seemingly inevitable digital future than what Sony is doing), and now Xbox Labs aims to take it even further. It remains to be seen if or how Xbox will look to monetize its Xbox Labs offerings, be it via an upfront cost, in-game microtransactions, or in-game-ad-based revenue.
The Xbox Labs announcement continues a busy stretch for Xbox, which revealed its entertainment-industry-focused Xbox XP arm last week.
Here's Sharma's memo to the team (also posted to Xbox Wire) in full:
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it?
item.description:
The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it?
Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie came out in 1994, the same year that the so-bad-it's-good live-action film with Jean-Claude Van Damme and Raul Julia was released. And while the highly-quotable (“For me, it was Tuesday”) live-action flick is a larger part of the public consciousness, most Street Fighter fans will agree that the animated movie blows it out of the water.
The animated movie doesn’t follow the World Warrior tournament seen in the game; instead, it focuses on Bison tracking down strong warriors using an army of cyborgs in an attempt to capture them for his own nefarious purposes. It’s not an official part of the official Street Fighter lore (which, admittedly, is quite confusing and convoluted), but it features some fantastic fights and, of course, the debut of Violent Ken (an evil version of the character corrupted by M. Bison's Psycho Power).
You’ve likely seen some GIFs from this movie floating around the internet over the years, and that’s no coincidence. The animation in this flick is simply fantastic, especially where fight scenes are concerned. One of the first ones we see takes place between Ryu and Sagat as a little backstory (which actually is canon); other iconic action sequences include Cammy’s assassination of a government official, Ryu and Ken’s final fight against M. Bison, and of course, Chun-Li’s iconic brawl with Vega.
Fights aside, one of the reasons the animated movie is so deeply beloved by fans is that it stays true to Street Fighter’s colorful cast of characters. Just like in the games, Ryu is a deeply contemplative, compassionate man on a perpetual journey of self-improvement; Ken is decidedly more hot-headed but maintains an aura of discipline learned from master Gouken; Guile is a classic American military man whose stoic facade breaks into goofy moments now and then; Chun-Li is a badass kung-fu practitioner who manages to keep hold of her girlish, quirky side; and Bison is a menacing, gangster overlord whose Psycho Power makes him feel like a serious threat.
Given it was the '90s, this version of Street Fighter doesn’t shy away from blood and nudity. In fact, there’s a fairly gratuitous shower scene that highlights Chun-Li’s physique, directly after which she tousles with Vega in a brutal, bloody battle. It’s not a family-friendly film, but it’s possibly the most accurate depiction of what the Street Fighter universe would actually be like if psycho-powered dictators and super-powered martial artists actually roamed the world.
Since it's an animated movie, it's also easier to sell the believability of its overall premise. Live-action adaptations have the challenge of making larger-than-life moves like E. Honda's Sumo Headbutt or Chun-Li's Spinning Bird Kick look realistic enough to fit into the real world; animated movies have the luxury of getting to bypass this, giving artists far more creative freedom in translating these moments from concept to page. This is one of the key reasons why the Street Fighter II animated movie pulls things off so well, and it set the standard for other adaptations in the years to come.
It'd be remiss not to mention the other animated Street Fighter films and series that exist, as well. The Street Fighter Alpha animated movie is a visual spectacle that unfortunately falls flat where story is concerned; the Street Fighter II V anime series is painful to watch, and we won't even get into the mess that was the American cartoon (though it also has some pretty quotable moments). It's clear, though, that the 1994 animated movie is the one to watch out of the lot, and as a diehard Street Fighter fan, I'd argue that it's required viewing if you're trying to get into the franchise.
Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie is available to watch on Crunchyroll, Pluto TV, and Amazon Prime Video at the time of writing this piece. It’s absolutely worth viewing, especially if you’re wanting to learn more about the world of the games ahead of the 2026 movie (or if you just want some badass anime fights). If you’re keen on diving into the games, you can check out our breakdown of how to play each of them in chronological order, or read our article diving into the nearly forty-year-old history of this iconic fighting game franchise from beginning to end.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade.
item.description:
Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade.
The report comes from Insider Gaming's Mike Straw, who spoke to senior-level sources working on or around the football series. He noted that, although the series is performing well, sales have gradually declined entry to entry since its highly-anticipated debut in 2024. While this isn't inherently a bad thing (or unexpected, given the extreme hype around the 2024 title), costs associated with the game have been rising.
Per the report, in 2024, EA paid each player featured in the game $600, amounting to roughly $7 million total. Those costs have tripled, with NIL (name, image, likeness) rights for college athletes now costing $1,500 per player. As a result, EA spent roughly $20 million on its players with its latest game. EA also pays boatloads of cash to license bowl games, universities, and more, meaning tens of millions of dollars goes into just having the right to use certain elements in the game as opposed to raw development costs.
This has led to EA trying to monetize key areas of the game, including College Football's single-player modes. This led to extreme backlash earlier this summer due to the fact players felt they were being pushed to pay to efficently play single-player content. EA eventually bent the knee and reversed course, but noted that it would retool these options and bring them back in future entries.
One source told Insider Gaming that microtransactions were planned to return in future College Football single-player titles, and feared that it would anger players, pushing them away from a game that is trying to grow. While there are College Football games planned for the next few years, sources reportedly fear that the franchise may be on its way out.
"We’re not FC. We’re not Madden. We don’t make the money they do, and everyone knows it," a source told Insider Gaming. "But it’s at the point where if we don’t find a way to keep players around and, in turn, make more, we won’t have anything. Forget in 10 years, I’m scared about if we have a game by the end of the decade. Games aren’t getting cheaper to make, and there’s the real concern with all of us that EA’s going to streamline and just have a few key franchises and dump everything else."
Insider Gaming noted that not all of its sources shared these fears and some believed there is a strong future with the franchise. EA Sports' College Football brand is a spiritual successor to EA Sports' highly popular NCAA football series that thrived in the 2000s and early 2010s before legal issues surrounding NIL rights effectively killed it. There was a 14-year gap between NCAA's final game and the debut of the new College Football series, which led to an extreme level of enthusiasm from fans.
It led to College Football 25 raking in big bucks and becoming the second best selling game of 2024 in the United States, though it hasn't sustained that momentum year-to-year. College Football 26 was the seventh best selling game in the United States in 2025, with College Football 27 currently placed in 10th this year. Of course, College Football also doesn't have as much global appeal as something like EA's FC series, which means its sales are primarily made up in the US.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Brandon Sanderson and Brotherwise Games have officially launched the Kickstarter campaign for War of Roshar, a new strategy board game. Sanderson has been calling this "the big one" in the leadup to this campaign and the fans seem to agree. More than $1 million has already been pledged in the first day, with 23 days left to go.
War for Roshar will join a growing lineup of Cosmere board games in collaboration with Brotherwise. IGN had an exclusive first look at the game earlier this year and loved what we saw. It's a massive tabletop war game that strikes the balance between strategic analysis and abstract gameplay. The theme of the game is rooted deeply in Sanderson's Stormlight Archive series and includes a wealth of art from over 30 different artists.
If you're looking to back this project, there are a number of options available. The featured pledge, called Fifth Ideal, is what will get you pretty much everything. At $295 this tier includes the base game, the Champions Expansion, 3D components, custom card sleeves, and wooden tokens. You'll also get a few different miniatures for the Cosmere RPG, including Mistborn ones from Era 1 and Era 2 to go with the upcoming expansion of that game.
If you don't care about the extra add-ons for the Cosmere RPG, the other four tiers will get you some variation of these items. For just the base game, you can pledge $90 to get access to the retail version as soon as it ships.
As for when the game will actually release, the campaign includes an estimated delivery date of November 2027. This will likely vary depending on where your game is getting shipped to, but Sanderson has a reputation for delivering high-quality products on time for all of his crowdfunding projects.
This is far from the first crowdfunding project that Sanderson has seen enormous success with. Just earlier this year he launched a massive campaign for Hoid's Storybook Collection that ended up raising more than $11 million. IGN's Jordan Comstock went hands-on with those books after they arrived and had no regrets with his choice to back the project.
And prior to that project, Brotherwise game initially funded the Cosmere RPG via kickstarter back in 2024 with a whopping $15 million pledged. So while War for Roshar is off to a great start, we'll have to wait and see if it has the potential to become Sanderson's most successful crowdfunding campaign of all time within his Cosmere universe.

item.title: About a month after it debuted in NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 is now being added to Hogwarts Legacy, with a new, faster model.
item.description:
About a month after it debuted in NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 is now being added to Hogwarts Legacy, with a newer, faster model.
In a blog post, Nvidia announced that it is launching a new model for DLSS 5 that's — according to Team Green — twice as fast as the model that debuted in NBA 2K27 last month. While the basketball game will be getting an update that adds this new model, and thus improves performance, Nvidia is also bringing the neural rendering tech to Hogwarts Legacy and Where Winds Meet in November.
Nvidia has been hard at work getting DLSS 5 to run well enough that people will actually turn it on when they're playing games. It's not hard to see why that's a major focus; when I first tested the tech back in September, I found that it could absolutely cripple my frame rate at 4K on the RTX 5090. It wasn't long ago, either, that Nvidia debuted the technology at GTC 2026 in March, where it needed to run on two RTX 5090s to deliver a playable experience, and even then it was super limited.
Now, though, Nvidia claims the new model is twice as fast as September's model, and ten times faster than it was when DLSS 5 was first revealed. If that's true — and I won't know that until I actually test it — it makes sense that developers are now willing to add the feature to their games.
But unlike some of the deep-fried examples I've seen of DLSS getting modded into games, the Hogwarts Legacy examples Nvidia shared in its blog are a lot more subtle. Rather than completely changing the way characters look, like it did when DLSS 5 was first revealed, it mostly just looks like it balances lighting and subsurface scattering.
And I'm not alone there. Over on X/Twitter, NikTek posted a GIF of him scrubbing through an image comparison with DLSS 5 turned on and off, and noted how small of a difference it makes. He then wonders who would actually use it with such a minor visual change and a big performance hit. However, there were some folks who applauded the subtle changes, with jayv7s replying, "This is the correct way to use it, no exaggerated AI slop filters on top, just normal pure improvement."
However, the subtlety of DLSS 5 will ultimately depend on the developer. There are plenty of dials that devs can adjust to make the game look as natural as possible, or leaning in the opposite direction to make games look like some kind of nightmare ripped straight from Midjourney. However, it is at least a little bit reassuring that in NBA 2K27 and now in Hogwarts Legacy, the developers are at least trying to maintain the same aesthetic.
No matter how subtle it is, though, DLSS 5 does work by using AI to re-draw games, even though it is anchored by the geometry and color data provided by the game. That's definitely enough to turn some people off of this tech, but if the changes are subtle enough and the performance continues to improve at this pace, I can see it eventually getting added to more than one or two games.

item.title: Looking for your next gaming obsession? From relaxing adventures to terrifying horrors, here are 9 newly announced games from IGN Fan Fest: Fall Edition to add to your Steam wishlist.
item.description:
IGN Fan Fest: Fall Edition is rolling out all week with a ton of first-looks, exclusive reveals, and deep dives into some of the biggest games for PC, consoles, and mobile.
From co-op survival adventures, brand-new horror games, relaxing survival games, mysteries and even a chess-based shooter, here’s a look at 9 newly announced games that we think are worth a look.
Fall into a chill survival adventure with a talking campfire as your guide. Explore, craft, fish and hunt during the day, and ask your fire three questions each night. Choose wisely: Winter isn't the only surprise in this beautiful, hand-drawn world. Playable in cozy or realistic mode.
Akiiwan: Relaxing Survival Steam Page
Something is wrong with the swamp. Aquamorta is a first-person horror adventure set in a forgotten swamp town, where something ancient has twisted a community into hysteria. Explore abandoned buildings and corrupted waterways surrounding the town. Use an old map and compass to find your way, fish for the blood that keeps your airboat running, and learn what lurks beneath the surface. As you venture deeper into the swamp, you’ll uncover the story of what happened here and what is still missing.
Checkmate Protocol is a chess-themed third-person shooter with unique weapons, chess-themed movement abilities, and unhinged boss battles. Fight alone, or team up with an arsenal of rifles, handguns, and chainsaws to defeat waves of oncoming attackers. Coming soon to Steam.
Checkmate Protocol Steam Page
In most tower defense games you combine towers. In Crown Must Hold you combine empires.
Every empire is a system of its own, with its own buildings and its own rules for how they work together. You take yours into a procedurally generated frontier, equip them with items that pull the run in a direction, and amplify the whole build with the biomes you claim as you expand. Push out for the resources you need and the undead get a longer front to hit you along.
A five-region campaign unlocks a new empire, biome and castle with every region cleared, then opens into Endless Mode.
Crown Must Hold Steam Page
Return to Azure City and join Justina in solving one of the biggest mysteries yet in Paper Perjury 2: Shadow of Justice. This upcoming detective visual novel is a follow-up to Paper Perjury by Paper Cat Games. Paper Perjury 2: Shadow of Justice is coming soon to PC.
Paper Perjury 2: Shadow of Justice Steam Page
Rotten Crown is a twisted real-time settlement manager where no problem ever fully dies. Grow your tiny kingdom, turn opposition into workers, balance the needs of humans and zombies, and make decisions no respectable ruler would ever admit to.
You can wishlist Rotten Crown on Steam now and sign up for an open playtest that will be held soon.
Rotten Crown Steam Page
Silk & Sorrow is a hand-drawn dark fantasy co-op adventure built exclusively for two players. The game tells the story of two orphans, Silk and Sorrow, who stumble into the Chrysalis, a hidden world where everything humanity has discarded ends up. Together, they must explore a haunting landscape built from the forgotten remnants of the world above, survive its twisted horrors and corrupted inhabitants, and bring light back to the Chrysalis. Silk & Sorrow can be played in both couch co-op and online co-op, with players needing to communicate, solve problems, and trust one another to survive a world where every step brings new dangers and unsettling discoveries.
Silk & Sorrow is coming to PC via Steam, with Chapter 1 releasing as a demo in Winter 2027.
Silk & Sorrow Steam Page
Float through the cosmos on a meteor as a Splizard in this cooperative survival adventure. Gather drifting resources, craft tools and expand your meteor into a traveling base. Swarms of bloodthirsty space mosquitoes lurk in the darkness, and powerful monsters guard the secrets of survival.
Step into the cockpit as mercenary pilot Ivan and fight alongside mech-with-a-soul Machine Spirit in The Forge: Steel Frontier, a mech action game coming soon. Dormant Dragon holds a strange and rare mineral and when wolves come for the ore, you and your mech must choose, and the planet's fate hangs in the balance.
The Forge: Steel Frontier Steam Page
For more IGN Fan Fest, be sure to check out IGN’s website, YouTube, and social channels throughout the week for more than 90 exclusive reveals across games, movies, TV, comics, and collectibles. It all leads to a massive livestream October 14 packed with game announcements, trailers, exclusive clips, celebrity interviews, and more.

item.title: Ryan Coogler's long-gestating reboot of The X-Files is a go, as Hulu has given the project a full series order.
item.description:
It's officially time to head down to the FBI's basement and reopen the X-Files. Hulu has given a full series order to Ryan Coogler's reboot of the iconic sci-fi TV series.
The new series is a collaboration between Disney's Onyx Collective, 20th Century Television, and Coogler's Proximity Media. Coogler wrote, directed, and executive produced the pilot. Coogler will executive produce the series alongside Jennifer Yale. Yale will also serve as showrunner. Other executive producers include Proximity Media's Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian and The X-Files creator Chris Carter.
The new series, which is frequently described as a "reboot" or "re-imagining" of the original show, stars Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel as a new pair of intrepid FBI agents investigating cases the Bureau deems especially strange and bizarre. The series' cast also includes Steve Buscemi, Amy Madigan, Ben Foster, Devery Jacobs, Lochlyn Munro, Tantoo Cardinal, Joel D. Montgrand, and Sofia Grace Clifton.
It's unclear whether the new series acts as a sequel to the original or a complete reboot, and whether David Duchovny and Gillian Anderson might reprise their roles as Agents Fox Mulder and Dana Scully, respectively. For their part, both actors have expressed an interest in returning, with Duchovny confirming he's had talks with Coogler.
“I’ve loved ‘The X-Files’ for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler in a statement. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.”
There's no word on a release date for the new X-Files yet. The show's pilot was filmed earlier this year, and presumably production on the rest of Season 1 will begin soon, making a late 2027 release a possibility.
In other The X-Files news, Carter has noted a desire to continue the storyline of the original series, which ended with Season 11 in 2018. Hulu also recently debuted Carter's director's cut of The X-Files: I Want to Believe. Read IGN's review of The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankensteyn.
The franchise is also returning to comics in the near future, with Dynamite Entertainment revealing a new series set during the classic era of the TV show.
Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

item.title: It's no secret that World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular since entering its beta last month, but now, over 1 million characters have been made.
item.description:
It's no secret that World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular since entering its beta last month, but now, over 1 million characters have been made.
According to classicplus.io, a community website that snapshots data from WoW Forever, 1,003,125 characters have been made in the Classic Plus mode so far. That's a lot, considering that to even make a character you need to have access to the beta, which is primarily done by buying the $60 Skyborne pack.
But even though most people will have to buy access to the Skyborne race to play in the beta, the Skyborne aren't the most popular race on either faction. For both Alliance and Horde players, the fancy blue elves only represent 18.7% of characters created. Instead, for Alliance players, Humans are much more popular at 32.3%, whereas Horde players seem to prefer Undead characters, at 33.5% of the population.
It's important to remember that while 1 million characters might not seem like a lot in a game that had a peak of 12 million players 16 years ago, WoW Forever hasn't even launched yet. The full game doesn't come out until November 4, and anyone playing the beta now only has access to limited parts of the world. At the time of writing, the level cap in the beta is level 30, and characters will be wiped when the full game launches next month.
So, it's impressive that so many people are playing the game right now, knowing that everything they earn in the game is going to vanish in less than a month. It's a good sign for Blizzard, and suggests that when Forever launches, it's going to be incredibly popular, even if it has to go head-to-head with Grand Theft Auto 6, which launches two weeks later — though I imagine there isn't much crossover between the two games.
Even when WoW Forever first entered its beta last month, Blizzard developers were shocked at how popular it was. One developer even said the beta was putting up "the craziest numbers" they'd ever seen. However, Forever hasn't been free of its own controversies. Blizzard has cracked down on players' names, leading some to think they've been unfairly targeted. And, Blizzard is also cracking down on gold selling, leading to WoW streamers getting caught in the crossfire. But, Blizzard has also added the beloved "Kyle's Gone Missing" quest, even though it wasn't added until Burning Crusade, and everybody seems to love that.

item.title: After a few price increases, the PS5 will now set you back $599 for the Digital edition, but Sony has just announced a cheaper $350 console – but it's exclusive to Japan.
item.description:
After a few price increases, the PS5 will now set you back $599 for the digital edition, but Sony has just announced a cheaper $350 console – but it's exclusive to Japan.
In a blog post, Sony announced that it was launching a Japan-only digital 'Midnight Black' PS5 for 55,000 Yen, or approximately $350, on November 19, the same day as Grand Theft Auto 6. At this point, with hardware prices being what they are, launching an affordable console like this worldwide might genuinely break sales records. However, the console will only be available in Japan.
According to Sony, this model can "only be used with a PlayStation account that has the system language set to 'Japanese' and the 'Country/Region' set to 'Japan.'" While there might be a way to game the system if you're really committed to it, for most people, this version of the PS5 is effectively exclusive to Japanese users.
This isn't the first time Sony has released a cheaper PS5 for the Japanese market. Back in November 2025, Sony announced a digital PS5 at the same 55,000 Yen price that was similarly exclusive to Japanese users, according to Polygon. However, a lot has changed in the year since then, and it's not just the fancy new colorway.
Pretty much the entirety of 2026 has been marred by price increases at the hands of AI datacenters. This RAMageddon isn't going to let up any time soon, and has already caused Sony to raise the price of the PS5 and PS5 Pro here in the US back in March. And, now that used PS5 Pros are going for around $1,400, there's likely another price increase around the corner.
So, it's unlikely that Sony is going to announce a similarly-priced PS5 here in the US or in Europe any time soon. However, that 'Midnight Black' colorway doesn't exist here, with the closest version being the Black PS5 sold by Gamestop. But this new, slightly-different colorway is exclusive to Japan, and I'd love to see it released over in the US, even if it carries the same price as any other PS5.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: God of War Laufey is the next big game to get a collector box without the game itself.
item.description:
Following in the footsteps of GTA 6, God of War Laufey is the next big game to get a collector box without the game itself.
Sony has revealed the collector box for God of War Laufey, which costs $150 and includes a nice statue of Faye. Unfortunately it does not include a steelbook with a disc copy of the game, or any copy of the game, physically or digitally. Preorders open today at 10am PT through PlayStation Direct, and stock is limited, Sony warned. You can view a full breakdown of the box's items below.
Predictably, a lot of people are drawing comparisons to the game-less GTA 6 collector's box. However, some may be a bit more accepting of the value God of War is offering here. GTA 6's box includes a bunch of Vice City-themed merch, such as a pair of sunglasses, a hat, and a figure of a cartoon gator named Macca. It also costs a whopping $400, which is tough to swallow.
Many were critical of the fact that GTA 6's box didn't include a statue of Jason and Lucia, in addition to feeling like the box could've been cheaper if it didn't include certain items. So, God of War Laufey may not be as egregious to some fans given it is a smaller box with a statue of the protagonist. Still, it does feel a bit lacking compared to previous God of War collector's editions.
God of War Ragnarok's collector's edition included Thor's hammer, a steelbook (no game disc, though), DLC, a code for PS4 and PS5 copies of the game, and a handful of other trinkets. God of War 2018's collector's edition included a statue of Kratos and Atreus, a steelbook with a disc, a physical map, a litograph, and two small figures of Brok and Sindri, in addition to a bunch of digital content.
While this is likely supposed to be an add-on for people who are already planning on buying the game, it's disappointing that God of War Laufey's box doesn't at least include a complimentary upgrade to the game's digital deluxe edition, which includes special armor and weapons in the full game.
God of War Laufey – Collector Box will be available in "highly limited quantities" exclusively direct from PlayStation on February 16, 2027 for a recommended retail price of $149.99 USD/ €149.99/ £129.99. Preorders begin today, October 13, 2026 at 10am local time.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Disney has officially set a streaming release date for the live-action Moana movie.
item.description:
Disney has officially set a streaming release date for the live-action Moana movie.
The latest remake hits Disney+ on October 21. The move to streaming comes a relatively standard three months after the movie’s initial release in theaters, though struggles at the box office have prompted reactions from Disney as well as questions about the future of the studio's remake strategy.
Moana’s box office hardships go back to the movie’s opening weekend, when it barely managed to beat out the numbers of a previous Disney disappointment, Snow White.
Moana went on to gross just over $162 million domestically, contributing to a total global haul of $323.6 million. It’s currently the 16th highest-grossing movie of 2026, with a box office total below previous live-action remakes like Lilo & Stitch, Aladdin, and The Little Mermaid.
The numbers (and memes) were enough to spur reactions from a number of the film’s stakeholders. Maui actor Dwayne Johnson, who reprised his role from the animated film, has been open about his disappointment while admitting, “That’s just the way it goes.”
Disney has also openly acknowledged that Moana “underperformed." Disney president Dana Walden attributed some of that underperformance to the decision to release the live-action remake so soon after Moana 2. The animated sequel did fare much better, nearly tripling the box office total of its live-action cousin.
Unfortunately, the Moana remake also struggled to win over critics. IGN’s own 6/10 Moana review derided the film as a “frame-by-frame retelling of the Disney animated musical that doesn't do enough to justify being made.”
Still, the studio remains confident in the franchise as a whole: “Looking ahead, we expect the live-action Moana to be a strong title on Disney+, building on the success of the original film, which is one of the most streamed movies of all time, and extending the reach of the franchise, which now includes three films, a themed area at EPCOT, and a robust global merchandise business."
As it stands, the Rock himself has mentioned development on Moana 3, but there’s no word on whether Moana will continue getting the live-action treatment. Disney doesn’t seem to be doubting their strategy too much, however, with all eyes now on the studio’s next live-action remake: Tangled.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
